title: Electronics Fundamentals Module 3: AC Waveforms, Capacitors, Inductors & Transformers
overview: Covers AC sine wave measurements (Vpp vs Vrms), capacitive/inductive reactance, and transformer step-up/step-down ratios.
art: AC SINE WAVE (OSCILLOSCOPE) (?1)             CAPACITOR (C) vs INDUCTOR (L) (?2)(?3)
│◄─── Period (T) ───►│                 Memory Trick: ELI the ICE man

1.label: AC Sine Wave: Peak-to-Peak (Vpp), RMS & Frequency
1.what: Alternating Current reverses direction periodically. Oscilloscopes show Peak-to-Peak (Vpp), while multimeters display RMS (effective DC-equivalent voltage).
1.exam_facts: Vrms = Vpeak × 0.707 | Vpeak = Vpp / 2 | Frequency (f) = 1 / Period (T) in Hertz (Hz). US wall power is 120V RMS (~170V Peak / 340V Vpp) at 60Hz.
1.troubleshoot: If your DMM reads ~85V on a 120V AC line, make sure it's set to AC (~) and check if you're measuring a non-sine wave without a True-RMS meter.

2.label: Capacitors & Capacitive Reactance (Xc)
2.what: Stores energy in an electric field between two conductive plates separated by an insulator (dielectric). Opposes changes in VOLTAGE.
2.exam_facts: Measured in Farads (uF, nF, pF). Xc = 1 / (2πfC). As frequency goes UP, capacitive reactance (Xc) goes DOWN (acts like a short to high-frequency AC). ICE: Current (I) leads Voltage (E).
2.troubleshoot: Electrolytic capacitors are polarized (+ and -)—putting them in backwards makes them pop/vent! Always discharge big power-supply caps before touching.

3.label: Inductors & Inductive Reactance (XL)
3.what: A coil of wire that stores energy in a magnetic field when current flows through it. Opposes sudden changes in CURRENT.
3.exam_facts: Measured in Henries (mH, uH). XL = 2πfL. As frequency goes UP, inductive reactance (XL) goes UP (blocks high frequencies, passes DC easily). ELI: Voltage (E) leads Current (I).
3.troubleshoot: Inductors rarely fail shorted; they usually fail OPEN (broken internal wire) or overheated with melted enamel insulation.

4.label: Transformers & Mutual Inductance
4.what: Uses two coils wrapped around an iron/ferrite core to step AC voltage up or down via magnetic induction—with zero direct electrical connection (isolation).
4.exam_facts: Vp / Vs = Np / Ns (Voltage ratio equals Turns ratio). Power stays constant (Pin ≈ Pout), so stepping voltage DOWN steps available current UP! Does NOT work on steady DC.
4.troubleshoot: Check transformer windings with an ohmmeter (power OFF!): Primary usually has higher resistance than a step-down secondary. 'OL' (infinite ohms) means a blown thermal fuse or open winding.
